classification.difficultyReason: Identify named circle features directly from a labelled diagram.

content.prompt: In the diagram on the right, what parts of the circle are:

spec.description: Circle with centre O, diameter PQ and chord AB. Clockwise circumference order is A, P, Q, B. Source blue outlines and red centre marker are rendered in house black because their hues do not distinguish mathematical roles.
spec.mathematics: PQ passes through O. AB joins two circumference points without passing through O. The arc from P through A to B is minor; the arc from P through Q to B is major. Angular positions reconstruct the source topology and are not numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels, the centre marker, the circle and both intervals are permanent question givens; no feature names are supplied.

answer.worked: $O$ is the centre of the circle.
$OP$ is a radius because it joins the centre to a point on the circle.
$PQ$ is a diameter because its endpoints lie on the circle and it passes through the centre.
$AB$ is a chord because it joins two points on the circle.
The curve $PAB$ is the minor arc because it is the smaller of the two arcs joining $P$ and $B$.
The curve $PQB$ is the major arc because it is the larger of the two arcs joining $P$ and $B$.
